node.title: Re^2: Perl Script to Run other Scripts with proper pauses?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I agree that [doc://do] might be suitable and have advantages, but for the OP I have to point out some caveats: The code executed by the [doc://do] will also see package variables from the surrounding scope, and will be sharing globals like [doc://$/] with the rest of the code. If one of the scripts sets these variables to something (without properly [doc://local]izing it), it will affect all the other scripts. This is not the case with [doc://system], since it'll be a totally separate process. Here's how one might do that, with appropriatebasic error checking (see [doc://$^X], as well as [doc://system] for how to interpret [doc://$?]). It would be best if $scriptname were an absolute pathname.

system($^X,$scriptname,@args)==0 or die "$^X $scriptname failed, \$?=$?";

Of course, whether it is a good set-up to have one Perl script call several other scripts, instead of having one script (properly modularized) do it all, might be questionable in the first place.
